meta_home_title: Everr: know before your customers do
hero_lead: Everr keeps watch over your app. When a page slows down or something breaks, it tells you what happened, where, and why. No specialist team required.
hero_notice_1_what: Checkout is slow for 1 in 5 people
hero_notice_2_why: It started with the last release.
hero_notice_3_why: The person on call has the steps to fix it.
tour_heading: An app can be up and still let people down
tour_lead: Working is not the same as working well. These are the questions that matter on a bad day. Pick one and watch Everr answer it.

tour_4_question: Will we hear about it before they do?
tour_4_detail: Everr notices when things drift and tells the right people.
tour_5_question: The alarm went off. Now what?

setup_heading: You shouldn’t need an expert to know your own app
setup_lead: Seeing this much used to mean hiring specialists or becoming one: deciding what to measure, building the views, keeping it all current. Everr builds that experience into the product, and your AI coding assistant does the setup.
setup_step_1_body: Ask your coding assistant to add Everr. It works out what is worth watching, wires it in, and proves it works on your machine before anything ships.
setup_step_2_body: Ready-made views show speed, errors and demand from day one. They follow practices that took the industry years to settle on, so there is no blank page to fill.
setup_step_3_body: Get alerts worth waking up for, each with the steps your team agreed on. When something breaks, your assistant investigates with what really happened.
setup_chapter_1_question: Can my assistant set this up?
setup_chapter_1_detail: It plans the work, makes the changes and checks the result on your machine.
setup_chapter_2_question: What should I be looking at?
setup_chapter_2_detail: It looks at what your app reports, then builds a view of what moves with revenue.
setup_chapter_3_detail: It reads the alert, follows the evidence and comes back with the cause.

faq_1_q: Do I need to know anything about monitoring?
faq_1_a: No. Setup, dashboards and alerts follow established practices, so the decisions an expert would make are already made for you. You can change any of them later.
faq_2_a: Everr comes with skills for coding assistants such as Claude Code and Codex. Your assistant adds what is needed working straight from your repository, and a collector on your machine lets you check that data arrives before you deploy. If your app already speaks OpenTelemetry, you’re most of the way there.
faq_3_a: While you develop, a collector runs on your machine and the data stays local. In production, your services send it to the Everr cloud, into a workspace scoped to your organization. Everr is also open source, so you can run it on your own infrastructure.
faq_4_q: What can I send to Everr?
faq_4_a: Traces, logs, and metrics in one OpenTelemetry model, the same signal from your laptop to CI to production. Business events ride the same pipeline, so product and engineering look at the same data.
faq_5_q: How do coding assistants use Everr?
faq_5_a: Through bundled skills plus plain SQL via the CLI: {#code}everr local query{/code} and {#code}everr cloud query{/code}. Your assistant reads what your app actually did, no glue code.
faq_6_a: No. Everr uses OpenTelemetry for ingest, the Perses spec for dashboards, and a ClickHouse SQL surface for queries, all open standards. Your data, dashboards, and alerts are portable files, not trapped behind a proprietary agent or query language.

selfhost_heading: Run Everr on your own infrastructure
selfhost_lead: Everr is open source. The code is yours to use under AGPL-3.0, with no Everr license fee. You manage the infrastructure, updates, and backups.
selfhost_body: Your hosting costs depend on the infrastructure you choose.
pricing_faq_1_a: Only data we actually store counts toward ingestion. Logs, traces, and metrics sent to Everr but dropped before storage do not count toward your monthly usage.
pricing_faq_2_q: How does the query allowance work?
pricing_faq_2_a: We don’t charge separately for data storage, so each plan has a query allowance to keep usage fair for everyone. It measures the data your queries scan, not the number of queries you run. If you need a different allowance, {#link}contact us{/link}.
pricing_faq_3_a: Hobby keeps logs, traces, and metrics for 14 days; Pro keeps them for 12 months. Each event gets the retention period of your plan when it arrives, so changing plans affects new data, not data already stored. Read the {#link}retention guide{/link} for details.
pricing_faq_4_a: Yes. Hobby is free forever, with no credit card required. The included quotas are designed to be generous enough for several hobby projects.
pricing_faq_5_a: You pay the Pro plan fee when you subscribe. Ingestion above the included 300 GB costs €0.10 per GB. At each monthly renewal, you pay for that additional usage from the month just ended together with the plan fee for the month ahead.
pricing_faq_6_q: Can I downgrade at any time?
pricing_faq_6_a: Yes. There is no minimum commitment, and you can cancel your subscription yourself at any time. Pro stays active until the end of the current billing cycle, then the subscription ends. Additional usage charges are frozen when you request the downgrade.
pricing_faq_7_q: Can I control and predict my costs?
pricing_faq_7_a: Yes. Pro has a fixed monthly fee and a published rate for additional ingestion, so you can estimate your costs. Monthly budget limits will be available soon.
